title: Properties of Materials
seo_title: Year 5 Science: Properties of Materials Worksheets (Conductors, Insulators, Magnets)
standard_code: Year 5: Properties and changes of materials
standard_text: Compare and group together everyday materials on the basis of their properties, including their hardness, solubility, transparency, conductivity (electrical and thermal), and response to magnets. Give reasons, based on evidence from comparative and fair tests, for the particular uses of everyday materials, including metals, wood and plastic.
meta_desc: Free Year 5 science worksheets on properties of materials: hardness, solubility, transparency, electrical and thermal conductivity, magnetic materials and choosing materials for a job. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Hard or soft, see-through or not, conductor or insulator, magnetic or not.
body_html:
How to think about it

Materials are chosen for their properties.

  • Hardness, solubility, transparency, flexibility, electrical and thermal conductivity, and whether they are magnetic.
  • Metals conduct electricity and heat. Only some metals (iron, steel, nickel) are magnetic.
  • Plastic, wood, rubber and wool are insulators. Test properties fairly before choosing.
Example

Saucepan handle: which property?

It must not get hot

Answer: a thermal insulator, such as hard plastic

Example

Is aluminium magnetic?

Only iron, steel, nickel and cobalt are

Answer: No

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all metals are magnetic.
  • Thinking insulators only keep things hot.
  • Confusing hardness with weight.

faq.q: What are the properties of materials?
faq.a: Features such as hardness, flexibility, transparency, solubility, whether a material conducts heat or electricity, and whether it is attracted to a magnet.
No. Only iron, nickel, cobalt and alloys such as steel are magnetic. Aluminium, copper and gold are not.
A material that slows down the movement of heat, such as wool, plastic or wood. It keeps hot things hot and cold things cold.
